title: Seva: the guest sails home
hookLine: the guest sails home with plans for the poor
carry: seva: serve people as you'd serve god
tomorrow: how many lines does an old yoga book give the poses?

lines: LETTERS TO CHICAGO, AND TO INDIA.
cards: A thank-you text, typed and deleted three times, because the real thing is too big for a text. Now a stack of letters, the paper soft from handling. Some go to Chicago, to the family that took a lost monk in off the curb.
Some go to India, and those are full of plans: not for a temple, not for a fan club, but for the poor. The guest is packing up, and he's taking what he was given home to give away.

teach.b: His letters from these years are collected in his Complete Works. To the Hale family in Chicago he writes like one of the household.
To friends in India he writes about what he's seen: American schools, and, with real admiration, the education and independence of the women he meets. Then he turns it toward home.
India's poor, he writes again and again, have been forgotten, and serving them is the work. Behind that sits a moment with his own teacher.
Sri Ramakrishna once said, as his disciples remember it, that pitying people from above isn't enough: serve them as Shiva himself.

teach.h: SEVA: GOD IN THE ONE SERVED.
teach.b: That's seva, service, and in the Vedanta he taught it's a road to God, because the same divine Self lives in the one who serves and the one who's served.

Brother monks came from India to carry on his classes, and he sailed home. In 1897 he founded the Ramakrishna Mission, with a motto it still uses: for one's own liberation, and for the good of the world.

teach.h: WHO WAS GUEST, WHO WAS HOST?
teach.b: So who was the guest, and who was the host? In seva the question melts. Seen that way, the Hales served God in a stranger on their street.
He went home to serve God in the poor. Nobody was paying anybody back.

how: Ramakrishna Mission centers and many Hindu temples run kitchens, schools and relief work as seva, service offered to God in people.

s: Vivekananda's letters from America only praised India and criticized the West
he writes home with admiration about American schools and women's education.
Ramakrishna taught serving people as Shiva, not just pitying them
his disciples remember it as the root of Vivekananda's seva.
in Hindu teaching, seva is a way of repaying what you owe
it's service offered to the divine in the other person. nobody's keeping accounts.

games.q: your temple asks for volunteers to serve the community meal. a cousin says 'why? those people never do anything for us.' what does seva answer?
o: serving them is serving God. it isn't a trade.
only serve people who can return the favor.
just send money. serving in person doesn't count.
games.why: Ramakrishna taught serving beings as Shiva, and Vivekananda built a mission on it: seva is offered to God in the person, not paid back.

practice: Bring to mind one person who served you this year without being asked: a host, a teacher, a neighbor. If you pray, offer a silent thanks for the God in them. If you don't, just hold their face and wish them well.
Then choose one small service for tomorrow, for someone who can't pay you back.

wordCard.voice: Vivekananda in America: a guest who sailed home to found a mission of seva, serving God in people.

carryVoice: Your line: seva, serve people as you'd serve God. The guest took the gifts home and gave them away. See you tomorrow.
